issue.title: Unblock E2 again: a green macOS core, core cuts the steward really dispatches, and a cutover wait that tracks master
issue.description: sase-core master CI is green on macOS again, so the daily cut can merge and publish a core. The release steward counts only merge-capable release-plz runs as core cuts, so its CORE_LAG action proposes a real cut and a heal run never hides a failed cut. sase-1oe.4 waits on the core pin that origin/master names now, not on a frozen workspace pin, so it can rehearse and raise the E2 handover gate.

issue.title: sase-core master CI passes on macOS, and a core containing the fix publishes
issue.description: macos-core: find why wal_mode_probe_consumes_conversion_budget spends 750 ms to 1.2 s of a 250 ms budget on macos-latest. Fix the product if it overshoots its wall-clock budget, or fix the oracle if the overshoot is outside the budget's control, without loosening the bound. Prove that master CI is green on both OSes and that a merge-capable cut publishes a complete core after the fix.

issue.title: Only merge-capable release-plz runs count as core cuts for the steward
issue.description: real-cuts: the steward's cut facts drop push and six-hourly heal runs, which never merge the release PR. CORE_LAG then proposes a real cut, and a non-merging success no longer supersedes a failed cut. The cut_budget decision bounds how often the steward dispatches. Prove it with a live read-only --once.

payload.entry: Monitor aecm017a7yjz (sase-1oe.4--mon-0, WAITING CORE) is still running in workspace sase_10 and polls `python3 tools/ratchet_core_pin --check` against that frozen working tree. No sase-1oe.4 continuation is running (followup_agent is null). Confirmed from `sase monitor resume -h`, docs/reference/automation/monitor-operations.md, and tests/monitor/test_monitor_resume.py::test_resume_rejects_stopped_monitor that resuming a monitor stopped with `sase monitor stop` is ineligible (inspection-only) and stop never launches the recorded follow-up. Left the monitor running; the CORRECTED WAIT PROCEDURE note on sase-1oe.4 covers its next wait.

LOCAL FIX CHECKPOINT (2026-10-29 UTC): GitHub CI run 40726794062 reproduced the existing macOS failure at 961.12475ms for a 250ms budget; Ubuntu passed. The Mac host was unreachable. Replaced SQLite nominal busy_timeout waits with a per-connection busy handler using the operation’s absolute Instant deadline for WAL setup and store reads/writes. Added a deterministic simulated scheduler-oversleep test and routed wal_mode_probe_consumes_conversion_budget through with_write_store. just fmt passed. sase tool run check ff5b0cd52a33355cb6323e2456608053 passed: 5549 core tests, 405 gateway tests, 360 macro-LSP tests, and all remaining suites; the two affected tests passed. This is local-only evidence; the change still needs the host commit, green master ci.yml on both OSes, and the next scheduled release-plz cut to publish a complete core. Follow core_cut=wait; do not dispatch a cut.
